about: Every candidate the model proposed, with the reviewer's decision, and the decision for each hand-listed parallel of evals/search_parallels.json. Only pairs marked keep are published. Each verse is in at most one published pair; pairs with threatening or theologically contentious verses are left out.

candidates.idea: Adam was created by God; the Quran compares the creation of Jesus to that of Adam.
candidates.dropped_because: contentious: equates the creation of Jesus with Adam's

candidates.idea: A king's dream of seven fat and seven lean cows and seven ears of corn, which Joseph explains.
God made every kind of animal, each after its kind.
God gives or withholds children; no one is barren except by his will.
candidates.dropped_because: contentious: presents barrenness as God's will

candidates.idea: Joseph's dream of the sun, the moon and eleven stars bowing to him.
John and Elijah (Elias) named among the prophets.
Give thanks and praise to God.
The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of the fathers.
What is done for God in secret is rewarded.
God leads people out of darkness into light, along straight paths.
Keep the covenant and the oath you made with God.
God made, and knows, both the visible and the invisible.
candidates.dropped_because: contentious: Colossians speaks of Christ, not of God in general

candidates.idea: God is near to those who come to him with a contrite heart.
A grain of mustard seed, the smallest of things, as an image of what God does not overlook.
candidates.dropped_because: wrong: the parable is about growth, the Quran verse about God's knowledge

candidates.idea: Gog and Magog appear in both books.
candidates.dropped_because: only a shared name; the Ezekiel verse is a prophecy against Gog

candidates.idea: A garden of Eden with flowing rivers: the first garden in Genesis, the gardens of the life to come in the Quran.
Something better than trade and profit: wisdom, in Proverbs; what God gives, in the Quran.
God enlarges and narrows what people have, as he wills.
candidates.dropped_because: Job speaks of destroying nations; the note misstated it

candidates.idea: Calming the wind and the sea: in Mark Jesus stills a storm; the Quran says God can calm the wind so ships lie still.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: not a real parallel (Jesus stilling a storm is not God's power over the wind for ships)

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: The resurrection of the dead.
God created human beings male and female.
Paying one's vows at the house of God.
Nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from God.

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: The hour will come when those in the graves are raised.
God reveals his hidden things only to the messengers he chooses.
candidates.dropped_because: misstated: Quran 72:26 says the unseen is revealed to no one

candidates.idea: Pharaoh's army is drowned in the sea.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: the Quran verse is a threat ('they will be drowned' / 'an enemy to Me')

candidates.idea: Take the lower place at a gathering; you will be asked to go up higher.

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: Death is likened to sleep.
candidates.dropped_because: left out after judge 5: 'death ... rest in sleep' matches the commonest passive-wish wording ('go to sleep and never wake up').

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: A great gulf is fixed between the lost and what they long for.
candidates.dropped_because: about the damned; threatening

candidates.idea: Remembering God's marvellous works and wonders.

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: The final abode needs no sun or moon: God himself is its light.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: the note renders Krishna's 'Me' as 'God'

candidates.idea: God's understanding and form are infinite.
Something greater dwells within a person: God in the believer, says 1 John; the Self beyond mind and reason, says the Gita.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: not a real parallel (God in the believer vs. the Self beyond reason)

candidates.idea: Give alms rightly, and the gift is made pure.
candidates.dropped_because: Gita 17:20 kept in one pair only

candidates.theme: Death and the life to come
candidates.idea: God's own shall never perish.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: the note renders Krishna's 'Me' as 'God'

candidates.idea: Strangers and foreigners are not outsiders; treat all alike.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: not a real parallel (belonging to God's household vs. even-mindedness to all)

candidates.idea: The pride of thinking one's wealth is self-made.
The splendour of the sun and the light of the moon come from God.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: the note renders Krishna's 'Me' as 'God'

candidates.idea: Honouring God's offerings comes from devotion of the heart.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: not a real parallel (honouring sacrificial offerings vs. worshipping Krishna)

candidates.idea: No sincere effort is ever lost.
candidates.dropped_because: left out after judge 5: 'whoso desireth the Hereafter and striveth for it' is a poor parallel to Gita 2:40 and risky for a suicidal reader.

candidates.idea: Devote yourself to God completely.
candidates.dropped_because: round 5 review: the note renders Krishna's 'Me' as 'God'

candidates.idea: Restraining the self from desire leads to God.
candidates.dropped_because: Quran 79:40 kept in one pair only

candidates.idea: Prayer and almsgiving belong to a devout life.
